newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SKI JUMPING-GOLDBERGER SUSPENDED FOR SIX MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-GOLDBERGER SUSPENDED FOR SIX MONTHS.

text.p: Austria's Andreas Goldberger, twice a winner of ski jumping's overall World Cup, was suspended on Thursday for six months for using cocaine.
Austrian ski federation spokesman Josef Schmidt told Reuters the federation's disciplinary board had banned Goldberger from April 21 until October 20 at a meeting in Kitzbuehel.
Goldberger, the 1996 ski flying world champion, was also handed a fine of 100,000 Austrian schillings ($8,390)
"The board has suggested that the fine be donated to an anti-drug organisation," Schmidt said.
Last month, Goldberger admitted on Austrian television ORF he had tried cocaine once at a Vienna disco but dismissed accusations of having bought, sold and regularly consumed the drug.
He also told ORF police had questioned him and searched his house but that no evidence had been found.
The 25-year-old Goldberger is immensely popular in Austria and was voted the country's 1996 sportsman of the year.
